title: This Glacier Moves 150 Feet in a Single Day

scenes.text: A glacier in Greenland moves 150 feet in a single day.
It's called Jakobshavn, and it's about 40 miles long and over a mile thick.
At its summer peak, it was the fastest glacier ever measured.
Its front breaks off in towering icebergs, some of the biggest ever filmed.
Today its summer speed is more than four times what it was in the 1990s.
A river of ice that moves faster than you can see it. Almost.

description:
Jakobshavn Isbrae in Greenland flowed up to 150 feet per day in summer, the fastest glacier ever measured.
It is about 40 miles long and over a mile thick, and is now moving more than four times faster than in the 1990s.
What's the biggest piece of ice you've seen?

first_comment: Bonus: its front is so unstable it produced the largest calving event ever caught on film. How close would you stand to this glacier?
